method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (the text's no where it says no; NOTHING-kind answers where it does not); the dates in one module, the rules and exported questions in another, the cases in a third; one regulative rule (applying to the Supreme Court within the time allowed: 14 days under s 16(2), 48 hours under ss 21(3), 23(3), 24(4)) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.

seat: the family of the person who died: usually the senior next of kin, or another relative or close person, who may have to report the death, is told of decisions, may object to an autopsy or exhumation, may apply to the Supreme Court, may take part in or give evidence at the inquest, and may later bring a claim (cornt-family.l4)

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run cornt-dates.l4 ; l4 run cornt-family.l4 ; l4 run cornt-cases.l4
checks.result: 170 assertions written, 170 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07); a deliberately wrong assertion in a scratch copy showed as failed
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: The provisions the family of the person who died meets: s 3 (senior next of kin), s 11(2), s 12(1), (1A), (2), s 13(1), ss 14, 15, 16, 17, 21, 22, 23, 24, 37, s 38(2), (3), s 40(2), (3), s 43(1)(c), (2), s 44 (with s 44A(1) in the answer text), s 45, and the maximum penalties of ss 12(2), 13(1), 19(4), 32(2), 33(4), 36(2), 41(3), 43(2), 46. Out: machinery (Part 2 except s 11(2), ss 47-49, Schedules), duties of doctors, custodians and police (s 12(3)-(5), s 13(2), s 25), the coroner's powers and findings (ss 18-20, 34, 35, 39, 41, 42), reports to the Attorney-General and responses (ss 26, 27, 46A, 46B), Part 5 disasters except the s 32(2) offence. Reasons in NOTES.md.
